items.title: The exam has two parts
items.simple: The knowledge exam has two parts. Part one is road signs. Part two is driving laws and safety. You take it on a computer. Every question comes from the driver's manual.
items.official: The two-part knowledge exam is given on a computer and tests your knowledge of traffic signs, motor vehicle laws, and safe driving. Exam questions are taken from information in this manual.
items.mnemonic: Part one: signs. Part two: smarts.

items.title: All 10 sign questions right
items.simple: Part one has 10 road sign questions. You must get all 10 right. Miss even one, and you cannot go on to part two.
items.official: You must correctly answer all ten traffic sign questions in part one of the exam before you can take part two of the exam.

items.title: Part two needs 80 percent
items.simple: Part two is multiple choice. It asks about general driving knowledge. You must get at least 80 percent right to pass. That is at least 8 out of every 10.
items.official: Part two tests your general knowledge with multiple choice questions. You must answer at least 80 percent of these questions correctly to pass part two.
items.mnemonic: Part one: all 10. Part two: 8 of 10.

items.title: One try per business day
items.simple: You can take the knowledge exam once each business day. Did not pass? You must wait for another business day to try again.
items.official: The exam may be taken only once per business day.

items.title: Under 18: wait 15 days
items.simple: Under 18 and fail the knowledge exam? You must wait a full 15 days to try again. Fail on January 1? The soonest you can retest is January 17.
items.official: If you fail the exam and you are under age 18, by law you must wait a full 15 days before you can retake the exam. For example, if you fail the exam on January 1, the earliest you can take the exam again is January 17.

items.title: Three fails: driver ed first
items.simple: Fail the knowledge exam 3 times? You must pass the classroom part of driver ed before a 4th try. Some people may take a DMV-approved 8-hour course instead.
items.official: If you fail the knowledge exam three times, you will not be able to take it a fourth time until you complete and pass the classroom component of driver education. You may have the option of completing an 8-hour course based on the Virginia Driver's Manual and approved by DMV exclusively for satisfying the three-times-failure requirement.

items.title: Audio, languages, no translators
items.simple: You can hear the exam read aloud. It comes in many languages and in American Sign Language (ASL). So if your language is offered, you cannot bring a translator.
items.official: An audio version of the exam is available and the exam is offered in many different languages and American Sign Language. Therefore, translators may not be used for tests in offered languages.

items.title: No cell phone in exam
items.simple: You cannot use a cell phone during the exam. Put your phone away before you start.
items.official: When testing, you cannot use a cell phone during the exam.

items.title: Do the exam on your own
items.simple: Do the exam on your own. Do not get help. Do not give help. Do not get or share test questions or answers before the exam.
items.official: When testing, you cannot: get help while taking the exam; help another person taking the exam; try to get test questions or answers before the exam; give another person exam questions or answers.
items.mnemonic: No help in, no help out.

items.title: Hands at 8 and 4
items.simple: Sit up straight but relaxed. Think of the steering wheel as a clock. Put your hands at 8 o'clock and 4 o'clock.
items.official: Sit straight but relaxed and place your hands on the steering wheel. If your steering wheel were a clock, your hands should be at the 8 o'clock and 4 o'clock positions.

items.title: Grip with fingers and thumbs
items.simple: Hold the steering wheel with your fingers and thumbs. Do not grip it with your palms.
items.official: Hold the wheel with your fingers and thumbs. Avoid gripping it with your palms.

items.title: Red light: complete stop
items.simple: A red light means stop all the way. Stop at the stop line. No line? Stop before the crosswalk or the intersection. Stay stopped while it is red, unless a turn is allowed.
items.official: At a red light, come to a complete stop at the stop line or, if there is no stop line, before entering the intersection or before reaching the crosswalk. Remain stopped as long as the signal is red, unless turns are allowed.

items.title: Green light: go if clear
items.simple: A green light means you may go. But look first. Go only if the way is clear.
items.official: At a green light, you may go if the way is clear.

questions.prompt: The Virginia knowledge exam is given:
choices: Out loud by a police officer
On a computer, in two parts
questions.explain: The two-part knowledge exam is given on a computer.

questions.prompt: The knowledge exam tests your knowledge of:
questions.explain: The knowledge exam tests traffic signs, motor vehicle laws and safe driving.

questions.prompt: Questions on the knowledge exam are taken from:
choices: Information in the Virginia Driver's Manual
questions.explain: Exam questions are taken from information in the Virginia Driver's Manual.

questions.prompt: To move on to part two of the knowledge exam, you must:
choices: Answer all 10 traffic sign questions correctly
Answer at least 8 of the 10 sign questions correctly
Pass the road skills test first
Answer half of the sign questions correctly
questions.explain: You must correctly answer all ten traffic sign questions before you can take part two.

questions.prompt: Part one of the knowledge exam has how many traffic sign questions?
questions.explain: Part one has ten traffic sign questions, and you must get all ten right.

questions.prompt: If you answer one traffic sign question wrong in part one, you:
choices: Lose a few points but keep going
questions.explain: All ten sign questions must be correct before you can take part two.

questions.prompt: To pass part two of the knowledge exam, you must answer at least what percent of the questions correctly?
questions.explain: You must answer at least 80 percent of part two questions correctly to pass.

questions.prompt: Part two of the knowledge exam is made up of:
choices: A driving test on the road
questions.explain: Part two tests your general knowledge with multiple choice questions.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the knowledge exam is true?
choices: Part one needs 80 percent; part two needs every answer right
Part one needs all 10 sign questions right; part two needs at least 80 percent
Only part two counts toward passing
questions.explain: Part one needs all ten sign questions right, and part two needs at least 80 percent.

questions.prompt: The knowledge exam may be taken:
choices: Up to three times a day
As many times a day as you want
questions.explain: The knowledge exam may be taken only once per business day.

questions.prompt: If you fail the knowledge exam in the morning, you:
choices: May not retake it that same business day
May retake it right away at another computer
May retake it the same day if a parent signs
questions.explain: The exam may be taken only once per business day.

questions.prompt: If you are under age 18 and fail the knowledge exam, you must:
choices: Wait until the next business day
Wait a full 15 days before retaking it
questions.explain: By law, if you are under 18 and fail, you must wait a full 15 days before retaking the exam.

questions.prompt: You are 16 and fail the knowledge exam on January 1. The earliest you can take it again is:
questions.explain: Under 18, you must wait a full 15 days, so a January 1 fail means January 17 at the earliest.

questions.prompt: If you fail the knowledge exam three times, you:
choices: May take it again the next business day
Must pass the classroom part of driver education before a fourth try
Must pass the road skills test first
questions.explain: After three fails, you must complete and pass classroom driver education before a fourth try.

questions.prompt: If you are 18 or older and have failed the knowledge exam three times, you may:
choices: Complete a DMV-approved 8-hour course on the manual, then retest
Retake the exam the next business day
Use a translator on the next try
Skip part one of the exam
questions.explain: Adults who fail three times may complete a DMV-approved 8-hour course based on the manual.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the knowledge exam is true?
choices: It is offered only in English
You may bring your own translator for any language

questions.explain: An audio version of the exam is available.

questions.prompt: While taking the knowledge exam, you:
